# Redirect Users Based on Their User Roles
Pro Configure automatic redirects for users after login, registration, or logout based on their WordPress role, sending different user types to role-appropriate pages.
Last updated on Jul 17, 2026

Role-based redirection allows you to send users to different pages after they log in, register, or log out based on their assigned WordPress user role. This is useful when you want administrators to go to the dashboard, subscribers to see their account page, and other roles to land on specific pages relevant to their permissions.

## What You'll Need

User Registration & Membership Pro plugin installed and activated

User roles defined in WordPress (Subscriber, Contributor, Author, Editor, Administrator, or custom roles)

Destination pages created for each role's redirect

## Understanding Role-Based Redirection

Role-based redirection works differently depending on the event:

**Registration redirects**: Configured individually per registration form

**Login redirects**: Configured globally and apply across all login forms

**Logout redirects**: Configured globally and apply across all logout actions

## Individual Registration Form Specific

This feature allows users to be redirected to a specific page based on their roles. Users can be redirected after registration.

To enable this, go to **User Registration and Membership> All Forms > Registration Forms. **

Select a Form to **Edit > Form Settings > General**. You will find an option that says ‘Redirect after registration’. Now, select ‘Role Based Redirection’.

After selecting 'Role Based Redirection'. In advanced section inside General setting You can manually choose the redirection page for different roles.

## Redirection after LOGIN & LOGOUT

You can use this feature to redirect the users based on their roles after they login/logout. You can configure the Redirection Type from the Settings button given for each redirection.

### Redirection After Login

After enabling the Custom Redirect you can choose redirection pages for different roles after Login.

### Redirection After Logout

After enabling the Custom Redirect you can choose redirection pages for different roles after Logout.

## Redirect Users After Login And Logout

# Redirect Users After Login And Logout
Learn how to configure custom redirect URLs for users after successful login and logout actions using the User Registration & Membership plugin settings.
Last updated on Jul 14, 2026

Would you like to send users to a specific page after they log in and log out? User Registration & Membership allows you to redirect users to any page on your site or an external URL after successful login and logout. This guide will show you how to configure login redirection through your login form settings.

## Prerequisites

Before getting started, make sure you've installed and activated the User Registration & Membership plugin on your WordPress site.

## Accessing Login Form Settings

To configure login redirection, go to **User Registration & Membership → All Forms → Login Forms**. Then, click on the login form you want to edit to open the form builder.

Once you're in the form builder, click on the **Form Settings** tab at the top of the page.

## Configuring Login and Logout Redirection

Navigate to the **Advanced** tab within Form Settings. Here, you'll see the login redirection options.

### Step 1: Enable Custom Redirect

Scroll down to find the **Enable Custom Redirect** option and toggle it on. This activates the redirection feature for your login form.

### Step 2: Choose Your Redirect Option

Once custom redirect is enabled, you'll see a **Redirect After Login** and **Redirect after Logout **dropdown menu. Select one of the following options:

**No Redirection** — Users remain on the current page after logging in or logging out

**Internal Page** — Redirect users to a specific page on your website

**External URL** — Redirect users to a custom external link (requires full URL)

**Previous Page** — Redirect users back to the page they were on before logging out

**Role Based Redirection** — Redirect users to different pages based on their user role (requires User Registration & Membership Pro)

### Step 3: Configure Your Selected Option

For **Internal Page**: Select the destination page from the dropdown menu that appears. This page must already exist on your site.

For **External URL**: Enter the complete URL (including https://) in the text field that appears.

For **Previous Page**: No additional configuration needed — users will automatically return to their previous page.

For **Role Based Redirection **(Pro only): Select a redirect page for each user role from the dropdown menus that appear. You can assign different pages for Subscribers, Contributors, Authors, Editors, and Administrators.

## Saving Your Changes

Once you've configured your redirect settings, click the **Update Form** button in the top right corner to save your changes.

## Testing Your Redirect

To verify your redirect is working:

Log out of your WordPress account

Visit your login page

Log in with a test account

Confirm you're redirected to the correct destination

## Set Admin Approval After Email Confirmation Option for Registering a User

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/user-access-and-redirects/set-admin-approval-after-email-confirmation>

Admin Approval After Email Confirmation in User Registration

# Set Admin Approval After Email Confirmation Option for Registering a User
Pro Configure a two-step user verification process requiring both email confirmation and manual admin approval before granting site access.
Last updated on Jul 14, 2026

This guide explains how to configure a two-step verification process for new user registrations. Users must first confirm their email address, then wait for manual admin approval before gaining full access to your site.

## What You'll Need

User Registration & Membership Pro plugin installed and activated

At least one registration form created

Admin access to the WordPress dashboard

## Understanding the Two-Step Process

When you enable admin approval after email confirmation, new users go through this workflow:

User submits the registration form

User verifies their email via a confirmation link

Admin reviews the request

Admin approves or denies the user

User is notified and can log in (if approved)

This creates a secure, two-layer verification system that ensures both email validity and admin oversight.

## How to Enable This Feature

### Step 1: Access Your Registration Form

Log in to your WordPress admin dashboard

Navigate to **User Registration & Membership** → **All Forms** → **Registration Forms**

Click Edit on the registration form you want to configure

### Step 2: Configure Approval Settings

In the Form Editor, click on the Form Settings tab

Go to General → User Approval and Login Options

From the dropdown menu, select Admin Approval after Email Confirmation

Click Update form to save your changes

### Step 3: Customize Admin Approval Email (Optional)

You can customize the email that admins receive when a user completes email verification:

Navigate to User Registration & Membership → Settings → Emails → To Admin

Find Admin Approval Request Email with Approval Link

Click the settings icon to customize the email content

Add the {{approval_link}} placeholder to include the approval URL in the email

Optionally add {{form_name}} and {{denial_link}} placeholders

Click Save to update the email template

## How to Approve or Deny Users

After a user verifies their email, you'll need to manually approve their registration:

Go to Dashboard → Users → All Users

Find users with Pending status (these have verified email but await approval)

Hover over the username and click Approve or Deny

Alternatively, if you included the {{approval_link}} in the admin email, you can approve directly from the email notification.

## What Users See

After submitting the registration form, users will see a message prompting them to verify their email. The exact message can be customized at User Registration & Membership → Settings → Registration & Login → Messages.

After email verification, users will see a message indicating that admin approval is still required. They cannot log in until you approve their registration.
